dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: Now I can breathe easy here...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Perform Emberic Reconstruction.

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: Alright, let me give it a try...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Perform Emberic Reconstruction.

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: Oh dear... Shame. I don't think we have enough embers at our central hub. If we could gather enough of them, perhaps we could then construct various objects.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why do they call you the "Master of Anti-Self-Termination"?

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: That's all because of a math problem I posed. The problem goes like this: a group of soldiers refuses to surrender, viewing it as a matter of honor. So, they decide to come up with a set of rules to...

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: ...determine who among them would end the humiliation, and for whom. So, what manners of rules would ensure that one would be the last man standing?

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: It's probably due to this purely mathematical problem.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me about your era.

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: My era was the one that came after Istoria's. I'd never heard of the dragon that tore open the sky in my time.

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: We were not as wise as those from his era, because the angels no longer bestowed true secrets upon us.

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: After I found out that all our philosophizing, creations, and struggles were all for naught, the only consolation I had was...

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: That Istoria's era wasn't particularly rich or opulent by any measure. Our two eras were comparable in terms of quality of life, in fact.

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: A philosopher in despair turned competitive hedonist. What a heartbreaking tale.

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: In this sense, Istoria has shown tremendous strength. The pursuit of knowledge and record-keeping are such meaningless behaviors...

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: Yet he still exerts his mind to such ends.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: As for this big thing in front of us...

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: Oh, this thing here is called a Memory Core. How do I explain this... Simply put, it is a place where information about unknown civilizations is stored.

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: Civilizations that fall out of human memory also lose their meaning, and things that lose their meaning will also lose their original form. Eventually, all that is left are embers known as Memory Factors, left to await a new cycle that shall never come.

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: If only we had more of these embers! Then we might be able to reproduce a thing or two... Unfortunately, it looks like there isn't enough of them inside the Memory Core at the moment.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: As for this big thing in front of us...

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: Oh, this thing here is called a Memory Core. How do I explain this... Simply put, it is a place where information about unknown civilizations is stored.

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: If only we had more of these embers! Then we might be able to reproduce a thing or two... Say, would you be interested in giving it a try?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: #I'll see you again, {NICKNAME}.
